subject: Zenith Payments: intermittent egress slow-path & NAT port scarcity during private cutover
messages:
From: Tom Richmond <ops@zenith-payments.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Alicia Gomez <networking@zenith-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zenith Payments - intermittent egress slow-path after private cutover

Marissa / Redwood team,

We cut over our private link to Redwood Private (VPC peering + Equinix crossconnect) early this morning. Since the cutover we've seen repeated intermittent egress slow-paths to our downstream payment processors: increased TCP retransmits (SYN/ACK retries) and a handful of timeouts from our reconciliation workers.

Symptoms we observed: 
- Spike in outbound SYN retransmissions beginning ~08:10 PST and recurring every ~30-60 minutes.
- Certain destinations succeed but return with high tail latencies (1–4s) while others appear blackholed for short windows.
- TCP connections sometimes succeed after multiple retries (suggesting transient NAT or routing fallback).

We captured packet traces on our egress appliance and attached them (zenith-pcap-20280628.tar.gz). Also attaching a snapshot of our route tables and the cutover runbook, in case anything looks off.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing asymmetric routing or SNAT exhaustion on your side? This is impacting nightly batch jobs and we need a mitigation ASAP.

Tom Richmond
Sr. SRE, Zenith Payments
ops@zenith-payments.com
(650) 555-0128

Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith Payments - intermittent egress slow-path after private cutover

Tom — thanks for the detailed note and the captures. I've opened an internal escalation and looped in Marcus (network infra) and Mina (private deploys). We have the attachments and will triage immediately.

Immediate plan:
- Marcus to validate SNAT port utilization and NAT pool health on the Dedicated pool attached to Zenith.
- Mina to review routing and BGP advertisements across the Equinix crossconnect (confirm no route flaps/asymmetry).
- We'll look for MTU/fragmentation signs in the pcap and confirm whether packets are being dropped by an intermediate device.

Could you confirm two small items to speed triage:
1) Are you doing any TCP MSS clamping on your egress appliance? If so, what value?
2) Do the failing destinations share any common AS / next hop?

I've attached a short mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-zenith-v1.docx) so we can assign owners/time windows. We'll aim to have preliminary findings back to you within 4 hours.

—Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, Tom Richmond <ops@zenith-payments.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith Payments - intermittent egress slow-path after private cutover

Tom / Marissa — I've finished a first-pass analysis of the captures and infra metrics. Short summary of findings and suggested mitigations below.

Findings (from Redwood telemetry + Zenith pcap):
- NAT port scarcity: the Dedicated SNAT pool serving Zenith is at ~94% ephemeral port utilization during batch windows. When the pool exhausts, flows are moved to a fallback path that uses a smaller, shared SNAT set — this explains the intermittent success after multiple retries.
- Asymmetric routing: one of the Equinix crossconnects (to eqx-lax-2) is advertising more-specific routes to a downstream transit partner intermittently. That causes a subset of return traffic to traverse a different path without the original conntrack state. The pcap shows SYN from Zenith egress but SYN-ACK arriving back on a different egress interface in several traces.
- MTU/Fragmentation: I saw large payloads with DF=1 and ICMP 'fragmentation needed' on a subset of flows. That contributes to added retransmits when PMTU discovery fails.

Immediate mitigations (we can apply within the next maintenance window — request a 1-hour window tonight):
1) Provision an additional SNAT port block for Zenith (increase ephemeral range) — low-risk and reversible. Expected to eliminate port exhaustion immediately.
2) Temporarily pin Zenith flows to the primary SNAT pool (disable fallback) while we stabilize.
3) Work with Equinix partner to remove the more-specific advertisement or adjust BGP community to prefer the primary path. I've opened a ticket with them (see external ticket below).
4) Recommend Zenith enable MSS clamp at 1400 on their egress appliance to avoid DF + large payload issues until we validate end-to-end MTU.

Data/commands I looked at (for record):
- conntrack -S shows conntrack entries peaked consistent with described times (see attached).
- iptables nat statistics and SNAT allocation table exported to route-table-snap-zenith.json.
- pcap extracts indicate reverse-path mismatch for ~12 unique flows in window 08:10–09:00.

Can Zenith apply MSS clamp quickly? If you can't, we can implement an interim MTU rewrite on our edge for those destinations, but that requires a maintenance window to avoid intermittent packet reordering.

Tom — I'm happy to jump on an immediate call if you want. Otherwise propose the 1-hour window tonight at 22:00–23:00 PST to apply: SNAT pool expansion + pinning + BGP community adjustment request to Equinix.

Marcus Lin
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com
(415) 555-3182

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Tom Richmond <ops@zenith-payments.com>, Alicia Gomez <networking@zenith-payments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Zenith Payments - intermittent egress slow-path after private cutover

Tom / Alicia — short update and next steps after the maintenance window tonight.

What we did (22:00–23:00 PST):
- Added an additional 65k ephemeral port block to Zenith's Dedicated SNAT pool and pinned active flows to the primary allocation.
- Temporarily disabled the SNAT fallback to the shared pool while we confirmed stability.
- Submitted a formal BGP community change request to Equinix to remove the accidental more-specific advertisement; Equinix acknowledged the ticket and scheduled the change for 2028-07-01 02:00 UTC.
- We did NOT apply MTU rewrite on our edge; instead we requested Zenith to enable MSS clamp (1400) to avoid side effects during traffic shifts.

Outcome so far:
- Nightly batch window completed with no SYN retransmit spike.
- Tail latency to the previously impacted payment processors returned to baseline in the 3–4 hour follow-up observation.

Next steps / owners:
- Zenith: enable MSS clamp 1400 on egress appliance and confirm results (Alicia).
- Redwood (Marcus): monitor SNAT utilization for 72 hours; if stable, re-enable safe fallback with higher port buffer and close the ticket.
- Redwood (Mina): verify route consistency after Equinix applies the BGP change; report by 2028-07-01 06:00 UTC.

If the issue reappears we will schedule an on-call war room. For now, please confirm MSS clamp and we will keep a close watch. Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with a short postmortem once we collect full telemetry.

—Marissa
